info.name: Privilege MCP Client — Docker (BFF relay)
info.description:
Tests the Privilege MCP client flow via the BFF relay running on the local Docker stack.

The BFF handles everything: it discovers auth from the mcpgw WWW-Authenticate header, registers a DCR client, runs PKCE against mcpgw's own OAuth AS, and relays MCP JSON-RPC. These requests are plain JSON over HTTPS — no bearer token of your own.

SETUP:
  1. Run the demo stack: ./run-docker.sh (or docker compose --profile mcpgw up -d)
  2. Postman must trust the mkcert CA: Settings > General > SSL certificate verification OFF,
     or import the mkcert root CA from ~/.local/share/mkcert/rootCA.pem
  3. Sign in to https://local.ping-devops.com:4000 in a browser first — the BFF reuses
     the existing PingOne session for prompt=none silent auth. Without a session, auth/start
     will redirect through the PingOne login page instead (still works, just not silent).
  4. Enable cookie sync: Postman > Settings > Cookies — ensure Postman can read the
     connect.sid cookie from api.ping.demo:3001 (or sign in via Postman's browser).

FLOW:
  Run requests 0 → 1 → 2 in order. After request 2, open the authUrl in a browser where
  you are signed in to the demo app. The BFF callback sets the session. Then run 3 → 4 → 5.
  For OpenSearch, run 6 → 7 after the cmuir-opensearch Privilege app is registered.

NOTE: mcpgw_url points at the SE K8s cluster — this is correct even for Docker, because
  the local Docker BFF's PRIVILEGE_MCPGW_URL env var points there. The Docker mcpgw
  container (cyonproxy) is the legacy mesh proxy; only the SE binary emits WWW-Authenticate.

request.description:
Returns the current privilege MCP session state.

Key fields:
  oauth.authenticated  — true after a successful auth/start + callback
  config.mcpUrl        — which mcpgw the BFF is pointed at
  mainAppAuthenticated — true when the user is signed in to the main app
  tools                — non-empty after a successful tools/list

item.name: 2. Start Auth — get PingOne redirect URL

request.description:
Triggers the BFF to:
  1. GET mcpUrl — discovers WWW-Authenticate header
  2. DCR on mcpgw OAuth AS (registers a PKCE client)
  3. Build the PingOne authorization URL (prompt=none if main app session exists)
  4. Return { authUrl } for the browser to follow

AFTER this request: open authUrl in a browser where you are signed in to the demo app.
The BFF callback (/api/privilege-mcp/auth/callback) exchanges the code and stores the token.
Silent auth (prompt=none) completes without user interaction when the main app session is active.

A 400 'Client ID is required' means request 1 was skipped or the session was reset — send request 1 first.

exec: console.log('\n=== OPEN THIS URL IN A BROWSER ===');
console.log('If the main app session is active, it will redirect silently back to the BFF.');

request.description:
Calls tools/list on the MCP server via the Privilege gateway.

Requires auth (complete request 2 flow first). A 401/403 means the Privilege policy is
enforcing access control — that is the demo feature.

Expect: { tools: [...] } — the full tool catalogue from the banking mcp-server.

Calls a specific tool. Change 'name' to any tool from the tools/list response.

The DEMO VALUE here is watching Privilege enforce its policy:
  - 200 with result data: the user's policy grants access
  - 403: Privilege DENY — the policy blocked this tool call
  - 401: token expired or invalid — re-run request 2

A DENY from Privilege is the feature working correctly.

exec: console.log('403 — Privilege policy DENY. This is the demo feature.');

request.description:
Switches the BFF to the OpenSearch mcpgw app.

PREREQUISITE: Register the cmuir-opensearch app in the Privilege console first:
  AI Security > Agentic Apps > Add Application > MCP Server
  App name: cmuir-opensearch
  Backend URL (K8s): http://ping-mcpgw-opensearch-mcp-server/mcp
  Backend URL (Docker): http://opensearch-mcp-server:9900/mcp
  Auth Mode: Static Token (empty — opensearch-mcp-server is unauthenticated)
  Mesh Cluster: your registered gateway

After save, mcpgw exposes: /cmuir-opensearch/mcp
Full URL: https://ai-demo.ping-devops.com/mcpgw/cmuir-opensearch/mcp
Same PKCE flow as request 2, but now against the cmuir-opensearch app's mcpgw path. Open the returned authUrl in a browser.

Lists tools from the OpenSearch MCP server via the Privilege gateway.

Expect: tools like search_documents, index_document, list_indices — OpenSearch operations.
